\begin{exercise} \end{exercise}

1-1. Let $X$ be the set of all points $\left( {x, y}\right) \in {\mathbb {R}}^{2}$ such that $y = \pm 1$ , and let $M$ be the quotient of $X$ by the equivalence relation generated by $\left( {x, - 1}\right) \sim \left( {x,1}\right)$ for all $x \neq 0$ . Show that $M$ is locally Euclidean and second-countable, but not Hausdorff. (This space is called the line with two origins.) \end{exercise}
